## Introduction 

In this notebook, we are reverse engineering the story, [CEOs gave heavily during legislative session, exposing loophole in NC's fundraising ban](https://www.wral.com/archive/17716104/)

## Load libraries

Loading required libraries for this analysis.

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
install.packages('refinr')
options(scipen=999)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(refinr)
library(janitor)
```

## Load and Cleaning Data

In this section, describe the source of the data, write a basic data dictionary for data you are working with, and discuss any caveats or issues you discovered working with this data. 

```{r}
donors_nc <- read_csv("data/donors_nc.csv")

cleaned_donors_nc <- donors_nc |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(
    city = str_to_title(city),
    profession = str_to_title(profession),
    street_line1 = str_to_title(street_line1),
    street_line2 = str_to_title(street_line2),
    employer_name = str_to_title(employer_name),
    zip = str_sub(zip, 1, 5),
    date = mdy(date),
    amount = parse_number(amount)
  )
cleaned_donors_nc
```

## Sentences to Engineer
In this notebook, we are reverse engineering five sentences from the story.
I cleaned the data column and output of the date, zip code, and city name. 
### Sentence 1

* **Sentence text**: 
R.H. Barringer's board chair, Jasie Barringer, donated another $8,200 in-session, and Teresa Craig kicked in another $5,200 to Berger. The North Carolina Beer & Wine Wholesalers Association PAC gave $18,400 during the week before session and on opening day."

* **Analysis summary**: [Write up two to three sentences describing the results of your analysis.  Were you able to confirm the finding? If not, why not?] 

We were able to confirm the finding by looking at the date. The first donation I found was the was Teresa's donation of 5,200 which was on 5/18/18, by sorting by the date we can find the donations leading up to that date. Low and behold, Teresa's was there as previously mentioned, Barringer donated 5,200 that date as well as three 1,000 donations after (combining to 8,200), and when you look at the donations in the week leading up to it by the association, it adds up to 18,400 perfectly. 


```{r}
sentence_one <- cleaned_donors_nc |>
  filter(name_clean == "TERESA S CRAIG" | name_clean == "JASIE S BARRINGER" | name_clean == "NC BEER & WINE WHOLESALERS ASSOC PAC")
sentence_one |>
  group_by(date)

```

### Sentence 2

* **Sentence text**: Scott Prestage, with Prestage Farms, gave Moore's campaign $5,200 right at the end of session, after the General Assembly passed legislation meant to make lawsuits against hog farms harder to win. Going back to the beginning of the year, people connected to Prestage Farms gave Moore $31,000 in campaign donations. Half are dated two-and-a-half months before the session began. The rest came in the session's closing days or the day after the session ended.

* **Analysis summary**: [Write up two to three sentences describing the results of your analysis.  Were you able to confirm the finding? If not, why not?]
Yes we were able to confirm the findings, people associated with Prestage Farms would donate acround $31,000 to the Friends of Tim Moore. John, Scott, and WH Prestage would end up donating 31,200 exactly to the Friends of Tim Moore Campaign


```{r}
sentence_two <- cleaned_donors_nc |>
  filter(name_clean == "JOHN L PRESTAGE" | name_clean == "SCOTT J PRESTAGE" | name_clean == "W H PRESTAGE") |>
  filter(date >= "2018-03-01" & date <= "2018-06-30")

sentence_two |>
  select(name_clean, amount, date, committee_name) |>
  arrange(date)
sentence_two |>
  group_by(name_clean, committee_name) |>
  summarise(total_donated = sum(amount))
```

### Sentence 3

* **Sentence text**: [Paste in sentence to engineer here]
“This year's legislative session also saw significant donations from hog farmers and beer distributors, both industries with important legislation before the General Assembly. Senate President Pro Tem Phil Berger's campaign alone raised nearly $222,000 during session. Twenty-three people gave him the maximum allowed: $5,200.”

* **Analysis summary**: [Write up two to three sentences describing the results of your analysis.  Were you able to confirm the finding? If not, why not?]
I filtered to keep the dates of the contributions only during session then I filtered so that the committee name was to Berger. After I summed the total amount of contributions which was more than the original $222,000 that was claimed he nearly met. Then I filtered to see how many contributions there were at the max amount 5,200 and found that there were 28 times that we was given the max contributions. 


```{r}
sentence_three <- cleaned_donors_nc |>
  filter(date >= "2018-05-16", 
         date <= "2018-06-30",
         str_detect(committee_name, "BERGER"))

sum(sentence_three$amount)                                        

sentence_three |> 
  filter(amount == 5200) |> 
  distinct(name_clean) |> 
  nrow()  

```

### Sentence 4

* **Sentence text**: [Paste in sentence to engineer here]
“More than a third of the PAC money logged during session went to Rabon's campaign.”
Came from taking a look at the data and calculating the data that fills the criteria out of number of individual pieces of data or rows. It is important because it is crucial to the story to see where Rabon’s support comes from. 

* **Analysis summary**: [Write up two to three sentences describing the results of your analysis.  Were you able to confirm the finding? If not, why not?]
After writing up the code and puting in time frame filters for when the pac money was logged , then filtering who the pac money was sent to. It shows that the claim was right, around 33 percent of the PAC money logged during the session did go to Rabons campaign.

```{r}
# Put code to reverse engineer sentence here
sentence_four <- cleaned_donors_nc |> slice(14133:17097)
sentence_four <- sentence_four |>
  filter(str_detect(name_clean, "PAC")) |>
  filter(source == "candidates")
rabon_total <-  sentence_four |>
  filter(committee_name == "RABON FOR SENATE")
#I subtracted 250 here because there was one contribution that was sorted into the group from someone with the last name Pace. 
sum(rabon_total$amount) /(sum(sentence_four$amount) - 250) * 100

```

### Sentence 5

* **Sentence text**: [Paste in sentence to engineer here]
"There was a major bump during the first week of session this year for the state parties, but that's because three large donors – LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman, Durham investor Greg Lindberg and Lindberg's Eli Research company – donated $1.3 million that week to the state Republican and Democrat parties."
* **Analysis summary**: [Write up two to three sentences describing the results of your analysis.  Were you able to confirm the finding? If not, why not?]
First I sorted just from the dates of the first week of session by doing the same thing we did in the third sentence but this time taking it from the days of May 16 to May 22 as that is the first seven days of session. I then sorted from that time period for just donations form the three groups listed above. From that I just added all the amounts of the donations together which yielded an answer of $1.25 million. Although it's not exact, I still feel we can confirm this finding because rounded up does equals 1.3 million. 


```{r}
sentence_five <- cleaned_donors_nc |> 
  slice(14133:14630) |>
  filter(name_clean == "REID GARRETT HOFFMAN" | name_clean == "GREG LINDBERG" | name_clean == "ELI RESEARCH LLC")
sum(sentence_five$amount)
```
